slides.text: THIS CHANDELIER IS MADE OF PEOPLE
Sedlec, near Kutna Hora, Czech Republic. From outside: an ordinary church and graveyard.
In 1278, the local abbot came back from Jerusalem with a handful of soil from Golgotha. He scattered it over this cemetery.
Suddenly, people from all over wanted to be buried here. Then came the plague... and war.
The graveyard overflowed. Bones were dug up and piled inside the chapel. Somewhere between 40,000 and 70,000 people.
In 1870 the Schwarzenberg family hired a local woodcarver, Frantisek Rint, to put the bones in order.
He made their family coat of arms... out of bones.
The chandelier is said to contain every bone in the human body.
Then he signed his work. In bones. Visitors still come to see it today.
